title.narrative: Countering cross-border corruption and illicit finance to advance development

description.narrative: This project is aimed at curbing the movement of corrupt financial assets and strengthening barriers against illicit money flows. The project will deliver outcomes that directly align with and advance the UK FCDO’s strategic priorities in combating corruption and tackling illicit finance.1. The systems and mechanisms allowing the corrupt to launder, invest and enjoy their illicit gains are increasingly disrupted. Thematic priorities cover ownership transparency, enablers of cross-border corruption and money laundering, accountability for kleptocracy and high-level, grand corruption, and reforms in global financial centres. 2. Policymakers, enforcement actors and advocates receive insight and evidence from the cross-case analysis of investigative reporting. 3. Increased scrutiny of kleptocratic players and transactions. 4. Global networks of journalists and civil society have opportunities to access and exchange information and receive essential investigative support. 5. Investigations expose corruption and related forms of wrongdoing and inform anti-corruption action; 6. CSOs use evidence uncovered by investigative journalists to advocate for policy change; 7. Increased levels of legally actionable information on corruption are available for use by watchdog organisations, governments and international organisations. Value of the contract: GBP 3,000,000.00Partner - OCCRP
